mcq.s: Intel Core i9 is a type of _____.
mcq.x: Intel Core i9 is a series of high-end Intel processors (CPUs) with 8 to 24 cores, for desktops, laptops and workstations.

mcq.s: 'Microsoft Word' is an example of:
mcq.x: Microsoft Word is a word processor, i.e. application software (not an operating system or a device).

mcq.s: MS Word is used for:
mcq.x: MS Word is word-processing software used to create, edit and format text documents.

mcq.s: Word processing, spreadsheet and photo editing are examples of:
mcq.x: Word processors, spreadsheets and photo editors are application software – programs for user tasks – unlike system software such as the OS.

mcq.s: The basic unit of Excel spreadsheet where we enter data is known as:
mcq.x: In an Excel worksheet the cell – the meeting point of a row and a column – is the basic unit where data is entered.

mcq.s: Which application software is used for sending and receiving e-mails?
mcq.x: Microsoft Outlook is the e-mail client of MS Office, used to send, receive and organise e-mail along with calendars and contacts.

mcq.s: 'Adobe Photoshop' is an example of which type of general purpose application software?
mcq.x: Adobe Photoshop is a raster graphics editor – graphics software for image editing and photo manipulation.

mcq.s: A word document, video or MP3 is a:
mcq.x: A Word document, a video or an MP3 song is each stored as a file; the file extension (.doc, .mp4, .mp3) shows its type.

mcq.s: Which of the following file format is not a video file format?
mcq.x: MP3 (MPEG-1 Audio Layer 3) is an audio format; MP4, MOV and AVI are video file formats.

mcq.s: Which electronic device was used in Second Generation Computers?
mcq.x: Second-generation computers (1956-63) used transistors in place of the vacuum tubes of the first generation.

mcq.s: Which one of the following is the main electronic component of the third generation computer?
mcq.x: Third-generation computers (1964-71) were based on integrated circuits (ICs); the first used vacuum tubes and the second transistors.

mcq.s: Miniaturization of present day computers has been possible due to the use of:
mcq.x: The integrated circuit (IC) chip, invented in 1958, replaced discrete transistors and made the miniaturisation of computers possible.

mcq.s: The IC chips are made of:
mcq.x: IC chips are made of a semiconductor – usually silicon – on which transistors, resistors and capacitors are built.

mcq.s: ICs are classified on the basis of:
mcq.x: ICs are classified by the number of transistors per chip: SSI (3–30), MSI (30–300), LSI (300–3,000), then VLSI and ULSI.

mcq.s: The device by which data are transferred by telephone with the help of binary signals is:
mcq.x: A modem (modulator-demodulator) sends and receives computer data over telephone lines by converting digital signals to analog and back.

mcq.s: Which of the following performs modulation and demodulation?
mcq.x: Modem = MOdulator-DEModulator: it modulates digital data into analog signals and demodulates them back.

why: same fact as gc-gene-1c0644bd (a modem sends data between computers over telephone lines), added above

mcq.s: A modem converts:
mcq.x: A modem converts both ways: digital signals into analog (modulation) and analog signals into digital (demodulation).

why: same fact as gc-gene-1c0644bd (a modem sends data between computers over telephone lines), added above

mcq.s: A modem is a hardware device that interfaces:
mcq.x: A modem is a hardware device that interfaces telephone lines and computer equipment, letting computers exchange data over the phone network.

mcq.s: The form of information signal used in sending fax and e-mail is:
mcq.x: Over phone lines a fax goes as an analog signal and e-mail as digital data, so both forms of signal are used.

mcq.s: ______ is the process by which the receiver interprets the symbols used by the source of the message.
mcq.x: In communication (sender → encoder → channel → decoder → receiver), decoding is the receiver interpreting the symbols used by the source.

mcq.s: Which of the following is a connecting device?
mcq.x: Router, hub and switch are all connecting devices of a network: a hub broadcasts, a switch forwards by MAC address and a router joins networks by IP address.

mcq.s: ROM is a memory:
mcq.x: ROM (Read-Only Memory) can only be read: its contents are written at manufacture and stay even when power is off.

mcq.s: In a computer, the permanent memory is called:
mcq.x: ROM is the permanent (non-volatile) memory of a computer; RAM is temporary and is erased when the power goes off.

why: same fact as gc-gene-87b552db (ROM is the permanent, non-volatile memory), added above

mcq.s: A means of specifying location of data in memory is called:
mcq.x: An address is the number that specifies the location of data in memory; each memory location has a unique address.

mcq.s: CD ROM stands for:
mcq.x: CD-ROM = Compact Disc Read-Only Memory, an optical disc holding about 700 MB that can be read but not erased.

mcq.s: A name for the short term memory of the computer that is lost when the computer is turned off:
mcq.x: RAM (Random Access Memory) is the short-term working memory; it is volatile, so its contents are lost when the computer is turned off.

mcq.s: Which of the following is not true about RAM?
o: RAM is a temporary storage area
RAM is like hard disk storage
Information stored in RAM is lost when the computer is switched off
mcq.x: RAM is temporary, volatile primary memory whose data is lost on power-off – unlike hard-disk storage, which is permanent secondary storage.

mcq.s: Which is not a type of secondary memory?
mcq.x: RAM is primary (main) memory; SSD, hard disk and USB pen drive are secondary storage.

mcq.s: Which of the following is primary memory in Computer System?
mcq.x: RAM is the primary memory of a computer; hard disk, compact disk and pen drive are secondary storage.

mcq.s: Which of the following is an extremely fast, small memory between CPU and main memory?
mcq.x: Cache memory is a small, extremely fast memory (made of SRAM) between the CPU and main memory that holds often-used data.

mcq.s: Which of the following memories has the shortest access time?
mcq.x: Cache memory has the shortest access time of these – the processor reaches it faster than regular RAM, which is why it speeds up processing.

why: same fact as gc-gene-3d03ba1e (cache memory is the fastest and speeds up processing), added above
answer not sure: cache memory is itself static RAM, so two options overlap

mcq.s: Which one of the following is NOT a correct statement about flash memory?
o: It is used for information storage in devices like digital cameras
It can operate over an extended temperature range
It is cheaper than normal mechanical disk drives
mcq.x: Flash memory (pen drives, memory cards, SSDs) keeps data without power and uses little power, but per unit of storage it is costlier, not cheaper, than mechanical hard disks.

mcq.s: Which one of the following is not the language of computer?
mcq.x: BASIC, C and FORTRAN are computer languages; FAST is not.

mcq.s: Which one of the following is not a language of the computer?
mcq.x: ROM (Read-Only Memory) is computer memory, not a language; Java, C++ and Pascal are programming languages.

mcq.s: Which is not a computer language?
mcq.x: Paint brush is a drawing program, not a computer language; BASIC, C++ and Java are programming languages.

mcq.s: Which one of the following is computer high-level programming language?
mcq.x: COBOL, PASCAL and BASIC are all high-level programming languages (3GL), like FORTRAN, C, Java and Python.
